blocking_analysis.requirement: The gates need cargo/rustc pinned at 1.95.0. rust/rust-toolchain.toml pins channel=1.95.0 (any rustup-shimmed cargo demands that exact toolchain), and cmd/rustgatectl's msrv gate HARD-REQUIRES a rustup-managed 1.95.0 toolchain (`rustup toolchain list` must show it; absence FAILS the gate by design, per the tool's honesty contract). cargo build/test additionally needs a C linker for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; the template has no cc/gcc/clang/ld.
blocking_analysis.template_state: The accepted template ships NO Rust toolchain in any location and NO C toolchain (probe results above, read from real command output, probe exits 0).
blocking_analysis.network_path_closed: The accepted profile is --deny-network '**'; rustup/cargo cannot download anything in-sandbox.
blocking_analysis.no_standing_authorization_for_materializ: The 0125 precedent (tla2tools.jar) required an EXPLICIT owner decision approving the host-side tool download (protected/us009-us008-owner-decisions-2026-08-27.json, us006_tlc_in_sbx). That decision batch contains NO authorization for fetching or materializing a Rust toolchain. protected/us008-owner-pinning-tier1.json records rustc 1.95.0 only as a 'Linux x86_64 archive digest pending acquisition' for the x86_64 benchmark host — not acquired, and the wrong architecture for this arm64 sandbox. No other protected record or draft authorizes it (searched protected/*.json and drafts/).
blocking_analysis.conclusion: BLOCKED without improvising a new profile. Executing the gates in-sandbox requires either (a) an explicit owner decision authorizing host-side fetch (digest-recorded at fetch, per probe-before-wire) and digest-verified materialization of rustup + rust 1.95.0 aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu + a C toolchain into the sandbox, or (b) a Rust-bearing template revision accepted through US-007-style qualification. Neither exists today; inventing either without the owner is prohibited.
